title: Pluralisation ternary in the multi-output banding summary chip is unreachable (always renders "s")
description: The summary chip `{rows.length} banded output{rows.length === 1 ? "" : "s"}` is rendered only inside the guard `showBandingSummary && !singleRow && rows.length > 0`. `singleRow` is defined as `rows.length === 1 ? rows[0] : null` (line 28), so `!singleRow` is true exactly when `rows.length !== 1`. Combined with `rows.length > 0`, entering this branch requires `rows.length >= 2`. Therefore the inner `rows.length === 1` test is always false and the singular form `""` can never be produced — the chip always reads "N banded outputs". The ternary is dead: the singular arm is unreachable. It can be simplified to a constant `s` (or the condition removed), which also documents the invariant that this chip is the >=2 case.
evidence: BandingDetail.tsx:28 `const singleRow = rows.length === 1 ? rows[0] : null`; BandingDetail.tsx:42 branch guard `showBandingSummary && !singleRow && rows.length > 0`. `!singleRow` ⇔ `rows.length !== 1`; with `rows.length > 0` this forces `rows.length >= 2`, so `rows.length === 1` at line 43 is constant-false.
est_reduction: 1 dead sub-expression (the `rows.length === 1 ? "" : "s"` ternary reduces to literal "s").
behavior_preservation: Behaviour-identical: in every input that reaches this branch rows.length is >=2, so the ternary already evaluates to "s"; replacing it with the literal yields the same rendered text in all cases.
